target.title: fix(nodes): correct system.which examples
target.body:
Closes #103888

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators copying the `system.which` example from `openclaw nodes --help` or either node guide would get `INVALID_REQUEST: bins required` because all three examples sent the unsupported singular `name` field.

## Why This Change Was Made

All shipped examples now use the canonical `bins` array accepted by both the headless node host and macOS node. A focused CLI-help regression test keeps the displayed example aligned with that contract; the runtime does not retain an alias for the erroneous documentation shape.

## User Impact

Operators can copy the documented `system.which` invocation to verify node connectivity and binary availability without first correcting its JSON parameters.

## Evidence

- Before: real `openclaw nodes --help` output showed `--params '{"name":"uname"}'`.
- After: real rebuilt CLI help shows `--params '{"bins":["uname"]}'`.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx6yygvd6zjh16w1bkyptsae`: `pnpm test src/cli/nodes-cli.plugin-registration.test.ts` — 5 tests passed.
- Same Testbox lease: `pnpm check:changed` — core/core-tests/docs lanes passed, including typecheck, lint, guards, and zero runtime import cycles.
- `pnpm docs:list` completed successfully.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/cli/nodes-cli/register.ts src/cli/nodes-cli.plugin-registration.test.ts docs/cli/nodes.md docs/nodes/index.md` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview: clean, 0.99 confidence, no accepted or actionable findings.

AI-assisted: Codex implemented and validated this fix; the maintainer requested no transcript attachment.

target.title: refactor(qa): share Matrix flows across channel drivers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA Lab scenarios could select only one channel driver, which forced Matrix behavior to be duplicated when the same scenario needed both the live Matrix adapter and Crabline's Matrix provider bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the small shared foundation needed for stacked Matrix QA migration work:

- allow a QA Lab flow to declare multiple supported channel drivers while still requiring the selected channel to match;
- map portable QA actor and conversation identifiers onto Crabline's Matrix endpoint without moving Matrix behavior into the QA adapter;
- run the existing shared/per-room Matrix DM scenarios through either `--channel-driver crabline` or `--channel-driver live` using the normal QA Lab flow host;
- keep coverage-report commands runnable by selecting a concrete supported driver.

This is stack PR 1 of 4. It does not migrate the legacy Matrix scenario/profile catalog, switch release workflows, or remove `qa-matrix`. Those changes remain in stacked successors so this foundation can be reviewed independently.

## User Impact

No shipped Matrix channel behavior changes. QA maintainers can execute the same two Matrix DM session scenarios against Crabline or the live Matrix adapter without adding a Matrix-specific scenario executor.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox: `tbx_01kx4kvpngzvbd4ck5846cj4qy` (`silver-barnacle`).
  - Matrix Crabline transport tests: 2 passed, including outbound-only logical target restoration.
  - Multi-driver suite-planning and coverage-command tests: 5 passed.
  - QA Lab UI production build passed.
- Identical Crabline/live DM flows passed before the split on the same nine-file behavior slice. Re-running the CLI after rebuilding on current `main` was blocked by delegated Testbox sync omitting tracked `extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/cli.ts`; no changed file depends on Mantis.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh whole-branch Codex autoreview on `114bf82f34ea52da3f83551f8f58a1663a0505f4`: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Optional agent transcript omitted by orchestrator default because the user did not request inclusion.
